title: Incorrect entities for the device of ZDB5100 for zwavejs integration
body:
### The problem

I have a ZDB5100 that is a wall controller for zwave. This wall controller has 4 LED's and 4 Switches which are "linked" together.
Which means i can control the LED color and functionality to the LED. But i can also control the switch it correspond to.

What i get out of the integration is the switches plus an internal dimmer (number 5).
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33527165/114585552-0fd27900-9c84-11eb-99fc-39882a98fe12.png)

The problem here is i can control the LED light if its active or not but i cannot control the switch and the coloring of the RGB diodes in the device.

Basically i have a device with:
Binary Switch
Color Switch
Multilevel Switch 

Something seems to be working incorrectly since the switches are just for lighting the LED but when the switch is being triggered the entity doesnt change but i can toggle the LED on the device if i toggle the entity.

zwavejs2mqtt "devices"
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33527165/114586064-8d968480-9c84-11eb-8cd2-8444f7beb7af.png)


zwavejs2mqtt debug file attached
[zdb5100_debug.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/6305218/zdb5100_debug.txt)

I have been updating the device in the node-zwave-js and found that i cannot control the LEDs and switches correctly and i cannot make automations with the switches because it doesnt trigger by clicking the switch on the device.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.4.3

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
In HA, only `light` entities support setting color. The zwave integrations create `light` entities based on the existence of Multilevel Switch CC values. Therefore, currently only z-wave dimmer switches will expose a light entity. RGB z-wave devices supported by HA use a combination of Multilevel Switch CC and Color Switch CC values to control the brightness and color.

This device uses Binary Switch CC for light on/off and Color Switch CC for color. There is also a Binary Color Switch device type defined by the Z-Wave spec which would support this same behavior. This device is not one of those, but acts the same way. Personally, I have never seen a Binary Color Switch device before now!

In order for HA to support a Binary Switch device that supports RGB, at least two changes need to occur:

1. A discovery schema that detects a binary switch value plus color switch values on the same endpoint. In this case, the value would produce a light entity instead of the default switch entity.
2. Update the light platform code to handle either binary switch or multilevel switch values to control on and off. It currently assumes every entity supports brightness, this would need to be detected based on the primary CC. This part is fairly simple and relies mostly on the discovery schema.

The problem with your device is it does not follow the z-wave specification of a Binary Color Switch device. As I understand it, the behavior is dependent on a certain configuration parameter being set to a certain value. Any other setting will not produce the same behavior. Dealing with this dynamic behavior may not be impossible, but will be challenging and is it worthwhile? In addition, your device also allows setting color independently of the switch being on or off, right? In HA, you must turn on the light to set color, you cannot change color while it is off. Lastly, the control of the White channel is not supported by the SET_VALUE API that zwave-js provides and HA uses. Using the commandClasses API would be a huge departure from the current design and could possibly end up being unsupported. A better solution there would be if zwave-js could force a white value to be supported, if possible.

Given all what was said in the prior paragraph, I'm wondering what benefit do you think you'd derive from having a light entity? It seems like you have the most flexibility using the `zwave_js.set_value` service to independently change color, and the usual switch on/off control? If the usual HA behavior for light entities works, then it might be worth implementing for other z-wave compliant binary color switches (if they even exist...).

The parser for the service call is converting `'343434'` to an integer because it allows multiple types and converts them according to a priority of possible types, with integer being a higher priority than string. I don't know if there is a way to force it to be a string, but in this particular case it's possible to use the standard RGB hex string `#343434` instead.

The other suggestion would be to use the combined color target value instead of `hexColor`:

```yaml
data:
  command_class: '51'
  endpoint: '1'
  property: targetColor
  value:
    red: 34
    green: 34
    blue: 34
```

I used google translate, I think I get the gist of it. The translation says to use the "hot white" value to control the blink, ID: 0, which would correspond to zwave-js' `warmWhite` property key, the one you are trying to use.

First question: I assume you already enabled the configuration parameter (10) to control this value?

Second question: after enabling the config parameter, it might either require a re-interview, or an exclusion and re-inclusion. Does the manual mention anything like this? Have you tried a re-interview? Can you ask the manufacturer what the expected behavior is supposed to be regarding the report of supported colors?

The supported color values are reported when the device is interviewed. The problem is, HA will not allow you to set any value it doesn't know about, so until the driver tells HA about `warmWhite`, you won't be able to set it via the `set_value` service call.

This might be another case where HA is being too restrictive about value IDs and it causes more trouble than good. To me it looks like the driver does not care if you tell it to set a single color value that the device never reported as supported (it does care if you use the combined color value as given above). It is possible to test this theory with zwavejs2mqtt.

I'm not sure if there's anything in the driver that could be done to force a `warmWhite` value ID to be reported, but that would help as well.

comments.body:
> but I did not made an exclusion / inclusion but if I do this I know all parameters normally reset to factory default.

Well, that depends on the device. Some devices specifically require you to set some configuration parameter to enable functionality and the re-include it.

> no there is stil no mention about "warm white" in the device configs

The supported colors are reported by the device, it's part of the Z-Wave specification. This information is not defined any device configuration file. If this device does not report that it supports warm white, then it is not spec-complaint and is a problem with the device. It would be worthwhile confirming with the manufacturer about this. node-zwave-js attempts to be as spec-compliant as it can. It could be that the Fibaro hub has code specific to handle this specific device, many hubs do work this way.

> if you have any idea of how to try more with the Warmwhite then please send something I can try.

In zwavejs2mqtt in the Advanced dialog there is a Driver function control. You can write and execute driver code. Try this (replace 100 with your value):
```javascript
const node = driver.controller.nodes.get(55);
```
